message.reasoning:
I need to make a decision in this Monopoly turn.

I rolled doubles from jail and landed on Virginia Avenue. I have $389 cash and own both Virginia Avenue and Baltic Avenue. I am deciding whether to trade, mortgage, or end my turn.

Rolling doubles from jail placed me on Virginia Avenue, which I already own. Since the decision type is POST_TURN_ACTION_DECISION rather than a roll decision, I am not required to roll again.

Player p2 holds a dominant position with four houses on light blue properties and Boardwalk and Park Place. I am weighing whether to trade or mortgage.

Player p2 has $1,511 cash and one get-out-of-jail-free card. Player p1 is nearly broke with only $147 cash. The orange and green monopolies are split between players. Player p1 owns an unmortgaged Atlantic Avenue but lacks the other yellow properties.

Player p1 has mortgaged every property except Atlantic Avenue. Player p4 is bankrupt. I cannot build anything and have no monopoly. Circulating the board will likely bankrupt me from player p2's light blue and dark blue properties.

I am calculating exact rent values for the properties. With four houses, Oriental Avenue and Vermont Avenue each charge $400. Connecticut charges $450. Virginia Avenue charges $500. Player p2's light blue set would cost me over $400 per visit.

I have $389 cash. Player p2's dark blue properties charge $1,300 and $1,700 with four houses. I cannot afford any light blue or dark blue rent. I am on Virginia Avenue.

Rolling doubles from jail does not grant an extra roll in this ruleset. I moved to Virginia Avenue and will proceed with post-turn actions before ending my turn.

I am evaluating trade offers to secure a monopoly or survive. I cannot acquire the unowned Mediterranean Avenue through trading, so I must land there to complete the brown set. Even with hotels on both browns, the combined rent would not bankrupt player p2. The pink set requires St Charles and States from player p2.

Player p2 will not trade the pink set for Virginia Avenue. Player p2 has better monopolies and would not want to give me a threatening pink set. Even with houses on Virginia, the rent is too low to survive against player p2's dark blue properties.

Player p2 owns Indiana Avenue, completing the red set. Player p1 holds mortgaged St James and Tennessee. Player p2 also owns New York Avenue, so the orange set is split between players.

Player p1 owns the complete yellow set, but both Ventnor and Marvin are mortgaged. Unmortgaging them would cost roughly $297, which is too expensive for my $389 cash.

I cannot afford to buy the yellow set from player p1. Even one house on each property would cost $150, and player p2 would bankrupt me before the set paid off. Mortgaging both owned properties would raise only $110.

Mortgaging would not meaningfully help. I cannot afford to pay rent, so I will end my turn.

Player p1 might accept cash in exchange for mortgaged properties, but that would help them survive and potentially unmortgage yellows for rent over $800. I would receive undevelopable junk. My prior plan was to stay in jail and avoid funding player p2. I am now out of jail on Virginia Avenue, so I will likely die next turn.

I will keep my deeds rather than mortgage them. Player p2 cannot bankrupt me, so the only remaining hope is landing on my own properties or drawing a chance card.

Player p1's mortgaged properties collect no rent, so landing on them would cost nothing. The orange set is incomplete because player p1 owns St James and Tennessee, so New York Avenue charges only $16. I can survive the $200 rent on Penn Railway.

The next roll from Virginia Avenue lands on Penn Railway, Indiana, B&O Railway, and Atlantic Avenue. All of these spaces are safe for my current cash. I will end this turn now. The following turn I can move freely through the board without immediate danger.

I could buy the unowned Mediterranean Avenue for $60 and build houses on both browns. Even fully developed browns would not bankrupt player p2.

I cannot afford to build hotels on both browns. I can only place three houses on each property, leaving $29 cash. That would charge player p2 $270 total if they land on both spaces, which is not enough to bankrupt them. Player p1 is nearly broke, so even a full brown set would barely affect the game.

I am mapping the exact path to Mediterranean Avenue. I must pass the light blue properties with four houses, which will bankrupt me. I also need to avoid landing on Park Place or Boardwalk, since those would kill me immediately. The green properties are safe with base rent. I can survive one railroad charge.

I considered trading all my cash and properties for player p1's entire portfolio. That would give me the yellow set, an incomplete orange set, an incomplete red set, and the water works. Player p1 would still only have his unmortgaged Atlantic Avenue. I cannot afford to unmortgage every property in that package. A trade structured so I give player p1 little in exchange for their holdings is also unworkable.
